    WILSON SISTER RANCH, LLC’S REPLY TO EXCEPTIONS TO THE PROPOSAL
                             FOR DECISION

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

        COMES NOW Intervenor JG & Wilson Sisters Ranch, Ltd. (“Wilson Sisters Ranch”) in

the above-styled case, and pursuant to the deadline set by the Commission, files Reply to the

Exceptions of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation (“Applicants”) and Commission Staff (“Staff”) to the Proposal for Decision (“PFD”)

issued on August 20, 2026, 1 and respectfully shows as follows:

                                INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY

        Wilson Sisters Ranch files these Replies to urge the Commission to overrule the Exceptions

filed by Applicants and Staff and adopt the Administrative Law Judges’ (“ALJs”) recommendation

to deny the Application. 2


1
  Exceptions and Replies Memorandum SOAH Exceptions Letter Request, PUC Docket No. 59475, Item No. 59475-
6442 SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 (Aug. 20, 2026).
2

                                                     1
          Applicants and Staff attempt to circumvent the evidentiary record by asserting that

ERCOT’s Permian Basin Reliability Plan (“PBRP”) alone mandates approval. 3 It does not. The

ALJs correctly held that Applicants failed to prove project need under PURA Section 37.056 and

committed notice violations under 16 TAC Section 22.52(a)(4) by denying approximately 1,400

landowners their statutory right to pre-filing public meetings. 4 Applicants’ Exceptions largely

ignore the evidentiary collapse of their load forecasts, mentioning the dispositive S&P Global

study only once and brushing aside that 55% of their non-oil and gas forecast consists of unverified

officer letters. 5

         In the alternative, if the Commission grants a Certificate of Convenience and Necessity

(“CCN”), Wilson Sisters Ranch supports Staff’s Exception adopting Route 487 over Route 894. 6

Route 487 is shorter, saves ratepayers $16 million, and utilizes nearly four times more existing

transmission right-of-way (“ROW”). 7 Finally, under any routing scenario, the Commission must

reject Link J24 in favor of Link J27 to avoid an identified historic Spanish mine site containing

confirmed human remains and protect the residential setback of the Wilson Sisters Ranch. 8

         REPLES TO EXCEPTIONS TO THE PROSPOSAL FOR DECISION

      Applicants’ Exceptions on Project Need Fail to Establish Quantifiable Substantiation
Under PURA Section 37.056 and 16 TAC Section 25.101.
         Applicants except to the ALJs’ conclusion that Import Path 2 is not needed, arguing that

the PBRP recommendation is entitled to conclusive “great weight” under 16 TAC Section

Docket No. 59475, Item No. 59475-6471 (Sep. 2, 2026).

 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii)(II). 9                    Applicants’             argument       misstates   the   rule.   Under   Rule

25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii)(II), an ERCOT recommendation is entitled to great weight only if the projected

load growth is “substantiated by quantifiable evidence.” 10 Unlike the CREZ statute, HB 5066

contains no exemption relieving Applicants from proving public convenience and necessity under

PURA Section 37.056. 11 The ALJs correctly evaluated the record and determined that the

underlying forecasts lack quantifiable substantiation. 12

              A. Unverified TSP Officer Letters Repudiated by Commission Orders

                          Applicants’ Exceptions fail to disclose that 61% of the PBRP’s 11,695 MW non-

              oil and gas forecast is based on unverified Transmission Service Provider (“TSP”) officer

              letters (55%) or is entirely unconfirmed (6%). 13 Oncor witness Jared Gurley conceded

              under cross-examination that Applicants took no steps to verify this demand. 14 Crucially,

              on June 5, 2025, in Project No. 55999, the Commission ordered a Good Cause Exception

              requiring ERCOT to discount officer-letter loads by 44.6% (a 55.4% realization rate) and

              data centers by 50.2% due to historical overstatements. 15 Applying the Commission’s own

              discount rates slashes projected demand by at least 3,571 MW—wiping out over 67% of

              Import Path 2’s 5,270 MW safe loading capacity. 16 Applicants presented no analysis

              demonstrating project need once this Commission-mandated discount is applied.

              B. The S&P Global 2022 Study is Factually Obsolete

                          ERCOT performed zero independent validation of the 2022 S&P Global study,

            which was the sole source for the PBRP’s oil and gas forecast (11,964 MW by 2030). 17

           The study’s core premise—that producers had to connect to the bulk electric grid to reduce

           emissions—was disproven by S&P Global’s own October 2025 report confirming that

           Permian Basin upstream emissions fell nearly 20% between 2022 and 2025 while

           production rose 500,000 barrels per day without grid expansion. Furthermore, the federal

           net-zero executive orders underlying those corporate pledges were rescinded in January

           2025. Applicants’ Exceptions relegate this pivotal issue to a single footnote-style mention,

           offering no evidence to rehabilitate the study.

           C. No Power Available at Bell County East and 25 GW of In-Basin Generation
                    Applicants admitted in discovery that neither Oncor nor ERCOT analyzed the net

           generation position of Central Texas or evaluated whether Bell County East has surplus

           power available to export to west Texas. 18 ERCOT’s 2023, 2024, and 2025 Regional

           Transmission Plans confirm Central Texas is an import-deficit area requiring imports from

           the Coast. Conversely, uncontroverted evidence establishes 25 planned and announced in-

           basin natural gas generation projects totaling 25.16 GW of capacity—including the Texas

           Energy Fund-supported CPV Basin Ranch (1,350 MW) and Vistra (860 MW) plants,

           alongside 10,000 MW of private off-grid data center power (Chevron and Pacifico

           Energy)—dwarfing ERCOT’s revised 17 GW regional load forecast and eliminating the

           need for Import Path 2.

The ALJs correctly concluded that the “great weight” presumption does not apply, and even if it

did, the greater weight of the credible evidence is against ERCOT’s recommendation. Applicants’

exceptions on need must be overruled.

      Applicant’s and Staff’s Exceptions Regarding Public Meeting Notice Disregard
Mandatory Due Process
        Applicants and Staff except to the ALJs’ conclusion that Applicants violated 16 TAC

Section 22.52(a)(4), asserting that holding three open houses in June 2025 satisfied the requirement

to hold “at least one” meeting. 19 This argument completely undermines the purpose of the rule.

        The record establishes that after holding three meetings in June 2025 for 2,809 landowners,

Applicants expanded the study area northward and added approximately 400 miles of route links,

bringing roughly 1,400 additional landowners into direct project impact. 2021 Applicants held zero

supplemental meetings. As a result, one third of all affected landowners were completely denied

the opportunity to provide pre-filing input regarding community values and routing constraints.

        Application notice under Section 22.52(a)(3) does not cure this failure. Meeting notice

allows landowners to shape routes before they are filed; application notice thrusts landowners into

a high-stakes contested case under an expedited statutory clock. Furthermore, while 16 TAC

Section 22.52(a)(5) allows for a day-for-day extension to remedy notice defects, Applicants

refused to waive the 180-day statutory deadline under PURA Section 37.057, which expires

September 22, 2026, and is enforceable by mandamus. 22 Because the statutory deadline cannot be

extended to convene new public meetings, the ALJs correctly held that denial of the Application

is the sole lawful remedy remaining.

      Applicants Failed to Comply with the Current County Tax Rolls Requirements Under 16
TAX Section 22.52(a)(3)
        Applicant and Staff except to the ALJs’ finding of non-compliance with 16 TAC Section

22.52(a)(3), arguing that using tax rolls pulled between December 8, 2025, and February 23, 2026,



19
   Applicant’s Exceptions at 48-49.
20
   Id. at 43.
21
   Id. at 50.
22
   SOAH Proposal for Decision at 3.




                                                 5
 was sufficient for an Application filed on March 26, 2026. 2324

         The rule explicitly mandates that direct-mail notice be provided on the date the application

is filed to owners of land “as stated on the current county tax rolls.” Central appraisal districts

update rolls continuously. 25 Applicants’ reliance on stale data resulted in over three dozen

landowners receiving late notice or no notice at all. Key landowners (such as the Jones, Hunsaker,

Thies, Hoffman, and Haufler families) received direct-mail notice 60 to 67 days after filing, on the

eve of the Hearing on the Merits, while others (like Craig and Carleen Edwards on Link E12)

received no notice. 2627 The safe harbor provision of 16 TAC Section 22.52(a)(3)(F) protects

utilities from isolated returned envelopes; it does not excuse a systemic failure to pull current tax

rolls prior to filing. Thus, Wilson Sisters Ranch agrees with the PFD in that Applicant did not

satisfy the notice requirements, thus depriving numerous landowners of their due process rights.

                                                CONCLUSION

         Wilson Sisters Ranch respectfully requests that the Commission overrule the Exceptions

of Applicants and Staff, adopt the Proposal for Decision, and deny the Application.

         In the alternative, should the Commission grant a CCN, Wilson Sisters Ranch requests that

the Commission adopt Commission Staff’s Exception selecting Route 487, and under any

circumstances strictly reject Link J24 in favor of Link J27 to protect human remains and residential

setbacks. Wilson Sisters Ranch prays for all further relief to which it may show itself justly entitled.

                                                      Respectfully submitted,

                                                      UHL, FITZSIMONS, BURTON,
                                                      WOLFF & RANGEL, PLLC
